analysis:
Integration of the four units: the PR changes scripts/install.sh lines 307-309 so the release tarball is extracted with `(umask 022; /usr/bin/tar xzf "$archive" -C "$stage")`. The umask applies only inside the subshell, so the installer's own private-state creation (provider.toml, tokens, keys; A-008, A-003) is unaffected. The changelog, the docs/operations/provider-release.md edit (lines 411-414) and the new test in scripts/test-install-atomic.sh (head lines 474-481) match the code. The test runs the install under umask 077 and asserts fan helper mode 755 and pagedattention.metal mode 644.

Security reasoning: the staging directory is created by mkdir -p under the caller umask, so extracted files are not exposed before the atomic commit. Final modes 0755/0644 are not group- or world-writable, so no write exposure is added. They are world-readable only for public, signed release artifacts. The bundle SHA-256 check precedes extraction, and hash, codesign designated-requirement, fan-helper mode and smoke checks follow it unchanged, so those integrity controls are not weakened. The fan helper's 0755 check (T-044/T-045, TB-010) is restored for restrictive umasks, since a 077 caller previously risked failing the capability check. The absolute /usr/bin/tar slightly reduces PATH-hijack risk (T-013), and macOS is already enforced by the installer.

No trust-boundary, attestation, authorization, encryption or billing behavior changes. The prefix-cache threat T-041 is not touched. Unverified contracts (non-blocking): the platform-served byte-for-byte snapshot of install.sh outside this repo needs syncing, and the base-side install.sh text was only partially replayed (7 units omitted). The supplied patch for install.sh is complete for the changed lines, and I found no regression.
